On Mac, the Photos app does the same—drag the drive in, click Import, and it consolidates everything. Both apps run for free on their respective systems.

For outdoor use, LED is your best friend—uses less power and won’t bake your plants. Look for the “IP65” rating; that means water and dust stay out. Brands like Philips Hue, Feit, and Hampton Bay all make solid outdoor strings. If you want color, warm white LEDs avoid that cold-store look and mimic candlelight.

Perfect timing—late summer in wine country gives you long daylight hours and rolling hillsides. Since you want to skip early-morning starts and keep tastings relaxed, here’s a lean four-day plan that hits the prettiest back roads without rushing.
Lovely, thanks! Could you help me think through how much ground we can realistically cover in four days without overdoing it?

Totally—four days is enough to sample the best stops without turning the trip into a commute. A good rule of thumb is to stick to one “zone” a day, staying within a 40-mile driving radius, so the car doesn’t eat up half your afternoon.

A single, tidy copy of ten years of memories—smart plan. Think of it like putting all the loose puzzle pieces into one labeled box so nobody can lose them again.
That's helpful, thank you. Are there any free tools built into Windows or Mac that can handle copying all these photos in one job?

Yes. On Windows, the Photos app has a “Import” button that can pull everything off a phone or drive in one sweep; it keeps the original file names and creates a “Pictures” folder with today’s date. On Mac, Photos does the same, but you’ll need to unlock the import lock once it starts. Both programs also let you preview photos before they’re copied, so you can skip duplicates.

You can absolutely mix it all by hand in one bowl. The dough will feel denser than store-bought batter, but once it hits the oven it puffs up just fine. Stick tips: work the butter until smooth, then dump in everything else at once. Use a sturdy fork to beat the sugar in—no need for an electric mixer, and you’ll save yourself another tool to wash.

LED mini-incandescent strings are light on power, run cooler than old incandescent, and most won’t heat the plastic in summer. Brands like Starry String, Philips Outdoor, and the lower-cost AmazonBasics Outdoor LED have good track records. Pick warm-white (2700 K–3000 K) for that cozy balcony feel.

Once the peanut butter goes in, you’re just folding, so hand mixing won’t change the chew—just don’t overwork the dough or the bars tighten up like a shoebox.
